notes:
## Content
The page defines intersections and localized terms for two bands, gives the union/limit formulas (105)–(108), and proposes a flat/natural-like superscript for the flag terms. The lower-right NB describes initial and final segments of the flags; its starred footnote says their union is the whole flag and gives the empty-intersection condition.

## Reading decisions and remaining issues
The expected identity in the second line of (106) prompted examination of the connected-left relation. Its ink still admits subset or equality; no mathematical expectation was used to choose it. The suggested last neighborhood factor visibly has \(i_{n-1}\), with a separate minus and 1. The cancelled union in (107) instead ends in a clear capital \(L\); this literal form is kept as a possible slip in the abandoned draft.

The comparison beneath (105) has a wavy upright and a separate straight upright, marked (h), inside the lower parentheses. It has no downward arrowhead. The first limit's lower stroke remains underline/arrow doubt; the marginal (107) limit has a clear head, while (108) has a plain lower rule. The two upright equality bars under (106) stay vertical.

Three short bars in the Suggestion and a point-plus-bar in the footnote are preserved as written continuation marks. Six empty-set signs are axial \(\phi\). The NB's overwritten middle flag group cannot safely be replaced by plain dots; its reading and cancellation state remain narrow doubts. The retraced les/tous, edge-truncated drapea\unsure{u}, footnote initial La/la, proposed superscripts and three struck readings remain unresolved. The footnote's cancellation precedes the live est.

## Sheet
Handwritten text sheet; no title, date or authorial page number. Formula labels (105), (106), (107), (108), and internal reference (102) are present. The thin lower 97 is later foliation in another hand. Thirty-two principal written baselines are counted, including annotations and foliation. Plain \(V\) follows the shared encoding of the rounded manuscript letter; this is not a collation change.
### Root checks of the displayed set relations and the ordered-band reduction

In(106), intersecting V_J with X_L^* is unchanged by additionally intersecting V_L, because X_L^* lies in every neighborhood represented by V_L. Thus equality is mathematically available where the manuscript's heavy connected relation is read only from its strokes. This observation does not resolve the visual subset/equality doubt.

Conditional on the union description in(101) and the incomparable-pair emptiness established on095 in the metrizability setting, distributivity and the three cases j=l, j<l, l<j give the three unions in(107). For(108), use the actual definition J prec L on090: each element of J is below some element of L and each element of L is above some element of J. If l in L lies below j in J, choose j' in J with j' <= l and l' in L with j <= l'. Convexity of the two bands then gives l in J and j in L. Consequently the reverse-order pair intersections are already absorbed by the union indexed by J cap L. This checks that reduction and also explains why a flag meeting both bands starts in J and ends in L, with its J-members an initial segment and its L-members a final segment. No independent categorical colimit or homotopy proof is asserted here. See CHECK_EVENTS statement150-098-band-reduction.
